headline: Does Joker's 1996 Anti-Nazi Stance Make Sense?
post:
Hey superhero fans! Let's talk about a weird moment in comic history involving Batman's greatest enemy. According to Screen Rant, a 1996 crossover called Batman & Captain America featured a temporary team-up between the Clown Prince of Crime and the Red Skull. Once the villain learned his partner was a Nazi, he famously declared: "I may be a criminal lunatic, but I'm an American criminal lunatic!"

Similar sentiments popped up later in other stories, but this patriotism angle doesn't quite add up. After all, this is the same character who once became Iran's UN ambassador and has never shown any real devotion to American values. Plus, he has committed massive atrocities himself, like destroying and eating China's entire population during the Emperor Joker event.

To make sense of his anti-Nazi stance, the writer suggests it might work better if it stemmed from his love of pure chaos or nihilism clashing with fascist order. Still, drawing a strange moral line creates a problematic plot hole for such a dangerous criminal. 

What is your favorite comic book crossover? 

#Batman #Joker #DCComics
original_title: After 30 Years, Let's Admit This Iconic Joker Moment Is A Stain On The Character
